designSummary: Individually randomised, partially nested trial comparing group visits with individual reviews.
sampleSize: To detect a 4 mmol/mol difference in HbA1c with a standard deviation of 14, 80 percent power and two-sided alpha 0.05 needs 193 patients per arm. Groups of about 10 with an intracluster correlation of 0.03 give the intervention arm a design effect of about 1.27; applying it to both arms for simplicity gives about 245 per arm; allowing 15 percent loss to follow-up gives about 290 per arm, 580 in total. This exceeds what one practice is likely to have, so neighbouring practices are needed.
primaryAnalysis: Linear mixed model for 12-month HbA1c with arm, baseline HbA1c and practice as fixed effects and a random effect for group in the intervention arm only (partially nested), by intention to treat.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model for diabetes distress; attendance described by age, work status and language; hypoglycaemia episodes compared descriptively.
missingData: Multiple imputation under missing at random using baseline HbA1c, practice and arm; a sensitivity analysis with a pattern-mixture approach.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes reported with confidence intervals.
software: R with the lme4 package; analysis plan finalised before unblinding.
overfittingGuards: Adjustment limited to stratification variables and baseline HbA1c
Analysis plan fixed before data lock
summary: About 580 patients for 80 percent power to detect 4 mmol/mol with partial nesting.
